  "reasoning": "All eleven field answers agree with their own captured worked solutions. Completing the square gives q-60360: 2(x-1)^2=11; q-60356: 3(x+1/3)^2=19/3, so q-p=6; q-86413: 4(w+1/2)^2=12. For the unshifted tangent and cotangent arguments, consecutive asymptotes give B=\\pi/T, with B positive from the direction of each curve. The graph midpoints give D. Thus q-65448 has B=1/2,D=1; q-117796 has B=5/4,D=1/2; q-65550 has B=5/4,D=-3; q-79188 has B=3,D=3. For q-143677, the zero at x=\\pi/2 gives \\pi/3+C=\\pi/2 modulo \\pi, hence C=\\pi/6 in the required interval. For q-143670, the zero at x=7\\pi/4 gives 7\\pi/12+C=\\pi/2 modulo \\pi, hence C=-\\pi/12. For q-99119, the increasing graph has asymptote y=3 and passes through (2,4), matching current option 4. For q-99114, the increasing graph has asymptote y=-2 and passes through (3,-1), also matching current option 4. Each selected exponential image depicts the same curve as its labeled worked-solution image. Both exponential solutions contain an ancillary wording error: a horizontally shifted (0,1) becomes a point on the graph, not its new y-intercept. The actual final y-intercepts are (0,109/36) and (0,-15/8), respectively. These wording errors do not change the correct graph selections.",
